inspiration: An effect catalogue with four kinds: moving object, particle, joint (a link between two points, used for lightning, beams and trails), and a single camera-facing sprite. Each kind has its own creation path, and effect types get names in data while the code keeps numbers (docs/effect-data.md lines 3, 23, 26). A clean shape for our VFX catalogue (row 8).

A joint effect is a link drawn between two points and used for lightning, beams and trails (docs/effect-data.md line 23). For us it is a tether or lock-on line between a fighter and a target, with its own kind rather than a generic particle.

Item definitions are one file per item group, with the group taken from the file content and not the file name, a format version at the top, and names per language inside each item (docs/item-data.md lines 9 and 20; src/bin/Data/Items/). This matches the catalogue-as-runtime-source rule (row 20 and 21).
A per-model glow table keeps each item's glow as data rather than code (src/bin/Data/Effects/GlowColors.json). A type cue at a glance, set in one place.

A monster health bar is shown only for the selected target, and only while its health status is not zero (src/source/UI/Combat/MonsterHealthBar.cpp, the ShouldRenderSelected function; caller in src/source/UI/NewUI/Character/NewUINameWindow.cpp line 210). README line 43 says the bar was added after an attack. The rule to copy is about visibility, not art.
The client has a reduce-effects checkbox for higher frame rates and a details overlay with frame time and a per-frame graph (README line 14 and the overlay bullet). Quality fallback for row 16.

A winged mount that can fly is an item trait in the item notes: it flies as in the original client, and the server does not yet give it the flag (docs/item-data.md line 137). A mount with a flight trait is a clean reward idea for row 22 and the Pit.
Auto-reconnect is listed as a client feature (README line 51). For a fast duel, reconnect should restore the fight, not start a new one. Idea only.

briefs.label: Tether line between two fighters
briefs.why: One thin line between two points reads as a link or a lock at a glance, even at 375 px.
briefs.keep: a joint-kind effect drawn between two points, with its own creation path and a short life
briefs.change: a dotted, pulsing line in the team colour instead of lightning; it breaks when the leash is exceeded; no shared asset with the donor
briefs.ref: docs/effect-data.md line 23 (joint kind). Recreate as an original tether effect; do not copy the code or the effect names.

briefs.label: Target bar after the first hit
briefs.why: The health bar appears only when it matters: on the selected target, after the first hit, and never on an idle target.
briefs.keep: shown only for the selected target; hidden when the target's status is zero; shown after an attack
briefs.change: a segmented bar that fades after a few seconds with no hit; plus a tick mark at the bar's half point for the 375 px readout
briefs.ref: src/source/UI/Combat/MonsterHealthBar.cpp (ShouldRenderSelected); src/source/UI/NewUI/Character/NewUINameWindow.cpp line 210; README line 43. Recreate as an original target bar.

briefs.label: Winged steed with a short flight
briefs.why: A mount that can fly over the field is a visible reward and changes the field for a short time.
briefs.keep: flight as a trait in the item data, not a special case in code
briefs.change: a short flight with a landing ring instead of free flight; a large fan-shaped wing silhouette in our palette; flight ends when the rider takes a hit
briefs.ref: docs/item-data.md line 137. Recreate as an original mount; do not copy the item or its name.

briefs.label: Glow as a type cue
briefs.why: A glow tells the item type at a glance, and a single table keeps the cue consistent.
briefs.keep: one glow value per item model, set in one data table
briefs.change: a pulse pattern as well as colour (steady, slow pulse, fast pulse) so the cue works without colour; the table is keyed by our item types
briefs.ref: src/bin/Data/Effects/GlowColors.json (file present, values not copied). Recreate as an original glow table.

briefs.label: Four effect kinds with their own creation path
briefs.why: Each effect has one kind, so the code stays simple and the catalogue names what each effect does.
briefs.keep: four kinds: moving object, particle, joint, camera-facing sprite; names in data, numbers in code
briefs.change: our kinds are named by gameplay role (hit burst, aura, tether, marker); add a fifth kind for ground decals
briefs.ref: docs/effect-data.md lines 3, 23, 26 and the Kinds table. Recreate as an original effect catalogue.
